name: Seraiah
title: David's Scribe
summary: Seraiah served as scribe (secretary) during King David's reign. He was an important official in David's administration and was responsible for the king's correspondence and official documents. His name is mentioned in the list of David's chief officials.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among David's Officials
keyEvents.description: Seraiah is listed as a scribe in the register of David's most important officials and servants who helped him govern the kingdom.

keyEvents.title: David's Administration Is Established
keyEvents.description: After David had secured his kingdom, he appointed his officials, including Seraiah as scribe, to ensure a well-organized government.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In Chronicles the same position is mentioned, but the scribe is called Shisha there, who is assumed to be the same person as Seraiah.

keyEvents.title: The significance of writing in David's kingdom
keyEvents.description: As a scribe, Seraiah played a central role in documenting royal decrees, keeping annals, and handling diplomatic correspondence in the united kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Service under David's rule over all Israel
keyEvents.description: Seraiah served during a period when David ruled over all Israel and Judah, and he contributed to the administrative stability of the kingdom.
